findings:
🟠 [p3-fixtures-bare-tmpdir] MUST-FIX Three P3 fixtures in hooks/tests/test-identity-guard.test.sh (P3B `$TMPDIR/p3-bypass`, P3R `$TMPDIR/p3-remote-ok`, P3U `$TMPDIR/p3-unrelated`) use fixed names directly under a bare `$TMPDIR`, not under TEST_TMP as the spec requires ("each case builds its own fixture repo under TEST_TMP"). Impact, assuming hooks/tests/lib.sh (not in the diff) leaves TMPDIR ambient, as G5/G9's `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` wording implies: (a) with TMPDIR unset the paths become `/p3-bypass` etc., so mkdir fails, or as root the repos land in `/` where the bypass is not honoured; (b) with TMPDIR set the repos are never removed, so a second run hits "nothing to commit" (exit 1) in P3B and fails "P3 NC: autopilot.testIdentityGate=off under TMPDIR allows", and concurrent runs collide; (c) it leaves repo residue in shared TMPDIR, which this plan exists to prevent. Smallest remediation: build the three under `$TEST_TMP/` (or, if TEST_TMP is not under TMPDIR, under `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/p3-XXXXXX"` with removal afterwards).
🟡 [p3-push-cases-simulated] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The push RED/NC cases call `.githooks/pre-push` directly with synthesized stdin and fake remote-tracking refs via `update-ref`, instead of the spec's real `git push` to a local bare remote; `protocol.file.allow always` is set but unused. Excluded from blocking because the hook receives git's exact argv/stdin contract and the RED note records file transport failing with 128 in the implementer's environment; a real bare-remote push case should be added where transport works.
🔵 [pre-push-blank-line-loop] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `done <<< "$__PUSH_STDIN"` makes the existing qc-gate loop run once with all-empty fields when git supplies empty stdin (e.g. an up-to-date push), where it previously ran zero times. The loop body is not in the diff, so no concrete failure is shown; a `[ -z "$local_sha" ] && continue` guard there would close it.
🔵 [pre-push-per-commit-forks] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `test_identity_refuse_push_range` runs three `git log -1` calls per commit instead of the spec's single `git log` with both emails per line. Verdicts are the same, but a first push of a long history to a new remote will be slow; excluded as performance-only.
🔵 [pre-push-revlist-fail-open] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `git rev-list ... 2>/dev/null || true` yields an empty set when `remote_sha` is not present locally (a force-push over unfetched history), so nothing is judged. Excluded because G8 mandates fail-open on internal error and the spec defines the set as exactly that rev-list output.
